chunks.Name: Ch5
chunks.Text: In this chapter, we will discuss the use of GANs in medical imaging.

chunks.Name: Ch5
chunks.Text: First, I want to start with a warning that image-to-image translation is considered harmful

chunks.Name: Ch5
chunks.Text: due to the potential for failures having a negative impact on patient outcomes.

chunks.Name: Ch5
chunks.Text: There are many papers published in the last few years presenting models which transform between modalities,

chunks.Name: Ch5
chunks.Text: such as from an MRI to a CT, and claim to be able to save a patient from a radiation dose.

chunks.Name: Ch5
chunks.Text: These approaches are often using distribution matching, with techniques such as CycleGAN, which provides compelling results.

chunks.Name: Ch5
chunks.Text: However, if the distributions are not representative, or the networks are not perfect,

chunks.Name: Ch5
chunks.Text: then these networks can hallucinate a target image and, depending on how they are deployed, can mislead a physician.

chunks.Name: Ch5
chunks.Text: Let's look at an example. Here, the source domain is a signal from an MRI that was under-sampled to improve acquisition speed.

chunks.Name: Ch5
chunks.Text: Because of this, the doctor cannot inspect the source image.

chunks.Name: Ch5
chunks.Text: A model transforms this data into the target domain desired by the doctor, and the image looks realistic and healthy.

chunks.Name: Ch5
chunks.Text: The physician is convinced there is no need to investigate further.

chunks.Name: Ch5
chunks.Text: However, in reality, the model is biased and failed to create features which should have been present, such as a gigantic tumor.

chunks.Name: Ch5
chunks.Text: This is the output from a real model that was trained on biased data.

chunks.Name: Ch5
chunks.Text: Because we cannot have a dataset with all diseases, we will always be training on biased data.

chunks.Name: Ch5
chunks.Text: And because imaging like this is for a general diagnostic purpose, use of these models may be harmful for patients,

chunks.Name: Ch5
chunks.Text: as a doctor will think they are looking at the real image and draw conclusions from the presence or absence of features.

chunks.Name: Ch5
chunks.Text: Here are generated images from 11 different CycleGANs, all trained with a different biased ratio of samples with tumors.

chunks.Name: Ch5
chunks.Text: The model here is transforming from a flare MRI image to a T1 MRI image.

chunks.Name: Ch5
chunks.Text: If no tumors are present in the training data, we can see that the model tries to remove the tumor.

chunks.Name: Ch5
chunks.Text: And if the training dataset is all tumors, then the tumor is enlarged.

chunks.Name: Ch5
chunks.Text: Here, we consider tumors as a proxy for some unknown pathology that may be present in the data at an unknown proportion.

chunks.Name: Ch5
chunks.Text: However, there are many great uses for GANs in medical imaging, such as for representation learning using models like BiGAN, Ali, InfoGAN, DeepInfomax, or GibbsNet.

chunks.Name: Ch5
chunks.Text: A good example is Cytogan, which applied these methods to represent cell morphology.

chunks.Name: Ch5
chunks.Text: These methods can be used to incorporate unlabeled data for semi-supervised prediction tasks, as well as for exploring what variations are present to understand the biology.

chunks.Name: Ch5
chunks.Text: Another interesting approach is for semi-supervised segmentation.

chunks.Name: Ch5
chunks.Text: In this setting, we have a few labeled examples and then a large collection of unlabeled images.

chunks.Name: Ch5
chunks.Text: The example task here is GAN segmentation in colon histology.

chunks.Name: Ch5
chunks.Text: The idea of one approach is to match the distribution between segmentation outputs on labeled data with the segmentation outputs on unlabeled data.

chunks.Name: Ch5
chunks.Text: This will hopefully correct any artifacts that appear when segmenting the unlabeled data and improve segmentation performance overall.

chunks.Name: Ch5
chunks.Text: The objective function for this is split into two parts.

chunks.Name: Ch5
chunks.Text: One updating the discriminator and one updating the segmentation network.

chunks.Name: Ch5
chunks.Text: The discriminator is trained to tell the difference between the segmenter output on labeled examples and the segmenter output on unlabeled examples.

chunks.Name: Ch5
chunks.Text: The segmenter is trained to predict the ground truth segmentations in a standard way, as well as to fool the discriminator.

chunks.Name: Ch5
chunks.Text: The idea is that this extra term in the loss will improve the details of the segmentation to remove any artifacts.

chunks.Name: Ch5
chunks.Text: Another interesting approach is to improve model explanations.

chunks.Name: Ch5
chunks.Text: The idea here is to use the fact that models can hallucinate when matching a distribution to explain what image features could make the model predict more or less.

chunks.Name: Ch5
chunks.Text: To achieve this, they start with a classification model as well as an independent conditional autoencoder.

chunks.Name: Ch5
chunks.Text: The conditional decoder acts as an explainer function network that generates images conditioned on a level of disease.

chunks.Name: Ch5
chunks.Text: They apply three consistency terms to align the models.

chunks.Name: Ch5
chunks.Text: First, the autoencoder must generate realistic examples when you perturb the latent space.

chunks.Name: Ch5
chunks.Text: Second, the explainer function should generate perturbed images which are predicted at the same level as the conditioning offset used to generate them.

chunks.Name: Ch5
chunks.Text: Third, when conditioned on no perturbation, the generated images should predict the ground truth label.

chunks.Name: Ch5
chunks.Text: Third, when conditioned on no perturbation, the result is a very promising result.

chunks.Name: Ch5
chunks.Text: The model can simulate increasing or decreasing the heart size while not being trained on any segmentations of the heart or information about what cardiomegaly was.

chunks.Name: Ch5
chunks.Text: This direction of research is very promising.

chunks.Name: Ch5
chunks.Text: First in point, the deviation chart is a very smart 410-1-?"

chunks.Name: Ch5
chunks.Text: Thank you.
